key_insight: Bulk Cs2AgBiI6, a long-sought lead-free iodide double-perovskite, can be synthesized in phase-pure microcrystal and thin-film form by converting Cs2AgBiBr6 via anion exchange after removing trace moisture.
engineering_relevance: This enables a stable, lead-free halide absorber platform for perovskite optoelectronic devices, including solar-relevant photoconductive films.
method: Removed trace moisture to enable complete Br-to-I anion exchange into Cs2AgBiI6
Made phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6 films by flash thermal evaporation followed by anion exchange
evidence_signal: The product showed broad visible absorption, a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-IR photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, and photoconductivity confirming carrier generation and transport.
watch_item: The synthesis appears highly sensitive to residual moisture, so strict dry-processing conditions are critical for reproducibility and scale-up.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
